[hint_advisor_caption] Unfortunately, the supplies of Iron are not infinite, and each new level of the mine for expansion becomes increasingly expensive. It therefore makes sense to secure an external supply of this valuable resource. Find a city on the world map that sells Iron and conclude a supply contract with it. Hint: A trade contract can only be concluded with a king whose relations with your ruler is above 0. If their relations is lower, use joint hunting or political methods, such as Envoy Visit or Offering to the King, to improve relations.

[hint_advisor_caption] For the church to recognize your town, it must have more people living in it than in a small village. Reach a population of 40 people so that the Matriarch will recognize your town and send a Bishop to live in it. $ Provide people with housing, Flour, and Beer to support migration.

[hint_advisor_caption] Now that your city has grown stronger, it's time to think about expansion. Create your own State—either an alliance of cities or a vassal kingdom. To make this happen, you will need an army no weaker than those of your neighbors. $ Hire warriors in the Army menu (bottom of the screen) and train them at the Training Ground. $ Buy or produce weapons and armor for them. $ On the global map, select a city of one of your neighbors. The options for annexing it can be found in the Politics menu. $ Annex one of your neighbors as a vassal or as a member of your city alliance. Hint: There are only a few provinces on the world map that sell Iron.

[hint_advisor_caption] The Chancellery is operational, but its clerks are not assigned to any production. $ Select buildings and assign a clerk from the Chancellery as a manager. Hint: Zoom out maximally to see all building assignments.

[hint_advisor_caption] The Chancellery is operational, but the Paper supply has run out. Since each clerk's inspection costs one sheet of paper, the Chancellery's work halts when Paper runs out. Hint: You can see how much Paper is consumed daily in the Statistics menu.

[hint_advisor_caption]
Although <hint=hint_fleshwolf>fleshwolves</hint> tend to stay close to the trees, they sometimes attack workers, especially woodcutters and herbalists.

$ Set up <hint=hint_bld_patrol_sign_day>daytime patrols</hint> in work areas. Warriors will attack fleshwolves as soon as they see them. But remember: fleshwolves are quite strong opponents.
$ You can send lords on a hunt, but you can also gather a squad of warriors (Army menu) and attack the fleshwolves via right-click.

[hint_advisor_caption]
The larger your settlement, the greater the need for lords. To alleviate this need, you can hire a <hint=hint_tutorial_free_lord>free lord</hint> to help delegate some tasks.

Free lords are hired for 10 days, after which they will leave the settlement.

$ Wait for the free lord to arrive at the settlement with the Holy Caravan.
$ Select their portrait at the top right (next to the caravan master's portrait) and hire them.

[hint_advisor_caption] Tools are needed for upgrading buildings and producing complex items such as weapons and Paper. However, their production requires smelting Iron, which in turn requires Coal. $ Buy a book on the Coal Furnace, study it, and build this facility. $ Buy a book on the Workshop, study it, and build this facility. $ Create a task to Do until 10 for the production of coal and tools.

[hint_advisor_caption]
Your state has become the dominant force in the world, and you can <hint=hint_tutorial_emperor>crown</hint> yourself as emperor to win the game.

To do this, select the Coronation of the Emperor in your ruler's menu. Within a few days, you can expect a squad of <hint=hint_inqusitors>Inquisitors</hint> to attempt to burn your province to the ground.

This is the final challenge in the game, after which there is no return - you will either defeat the punitive squad of Inquisitors and win the game, or you will lose. In any case, the game will end.
